Think of **Formatting Console Output** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: System.out.printf() uses format specifiers to control output formatting
%d formats integers; %f formats floating-point numbers; %s formats strings
%.2f limits the decimal to 2 places; %10d right-aligns in a 10-character field
%-10s left-aligns the string in a 10-character field

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Formatting Console Output - Using printf for formatted output. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: Which method is used for formatted output in Java?
questions.explanation: System.out.printf() is used for formatted output, allowing format specifiers like %d for integers, %f for floating-point numbers, and %s for strings.

questions.question: What does the format specifier %d represent in printf?
questions.explanation: %d is the format specifier for integer values in printf. %f is for floating-point, %s is for strings, and %c is for characters.
